note: People you can walk up to and talk to. 'map' is a story chapter id or 'city'. City people stand by a place ('place') or at x/y. 'lines' are small talk; 'talks' are offers (first one whose 'if' passes, once per day). Talking to a story character raises your relationship a little, once a day.

people.name: Mama
lines: "{name}, you don chop? Go and wash your uniform."
"When I sell finish today, I go buy you Fanta. Small one."
"Read your book. Book na the only thing nobody fit collect from you."

talks.text: "You've eaten? Good. Come and help me at the stall this evening. Customers like a small child's face."

choices.result: You call out prices louder than the market women. Mama pretends not to be proud.

then.toast: Mama sighs and gives you ₦200 from her wrapper.

else.toast: "Pocket money? Is it me you're asking? Go and read your books."

choices.result: She listens while she sorts tomatoes. It's the best part of your day.

people.name: Daddy
lines: "{name}, this term I want to see A's. Not B's. A's."
"In my office, the files have been 'moving' for six years."
"Your mother says you're helping at the stall. Good. Trade is also education."

talks.text: "How was school? Did they teach you anything, or did you teach them?"

choices.result: Daddy explains long division with groundnuts. You eat the remainder.
He inspects it like an army general. Then he pays.

choices.text: Ask him about his work at the Secretariat
choices.result: "Files," he says. "Files and meetings. Study hard, so you can choose your files."

people.name: Tunde
lines: "I sell 40 sachets before school today. New record!"
"My mama say make I no follow Slim. Wetin you think?"
"When I grow up, I go get motor. Two motors."

talks.text: "My guy! Mama Put says she'll pay us ₦300 each to wash plates after school. Or we can go and play ball. Your choice."

choices.result: Soap to your elbows, gist with Tunde. Not a bad afternoon.
Tunde scores. You claim the assist.

choices.text: Plan a prank on the class monitor

then.toast: The monitor writes both your names in red.

else.toast: A toad in the monitor's bag. Legendary.

people.name: Slim
lines: "My guy, see my new shoe. My uncle for abroad send am."
"Teacher no fit catch me. I sabi the format already."
"Stay with me, you go enjoy."

talks.text: "I've got a Game Boy. JSS kids will pay ₦50 a game. You hold it during break, we split the money."

choices.text: Rent out the Game Boy for a cut

then.toast: Mrs. Bassey confiscates the Game Boy. Slim blames you.

choices.text: Get Slim to 'borrow' exam questions from the staff room

then.toast: The cleaner sees you both near the staff room cabinet.

else.toast: You know every question before the test. Your conscience knows too.

choices.text: Swap your lunch for his homework answers
choices.result: Full marks, empty stomach.

people.name: Headmaster
lines: "Tuck in that shirt!"
"Those owing fees, I'm watching you."
"Discipline is the road to success. And so are fees."

talks.text: "Ah, you. Make yourself useful: take these letters to the LEA office, and come straight back."

choices.result: "Good child." Two words from the headmaster feel like a medal.

choices.text: Ask about the bursary for good pupils

then.toast: A ₦3,000 bursary for your results! Mama frames the letter.

else.toast: "Next term, if your grades are high enough."

choices.text: Ask to ring the school bell
choices.result: Power. Pure power.

people.name: Pure water seller
lines: "Pure water! Cold pure water! ₦20!"
"You wan sell for me? I go give you 20 sachets on credit."

talks.text: "Small boy/small girl, you wan help me sell 20 sachets?"

choices.result: Hot sun, cold water. ₦300 profit. Not bad for nine years old.

people.name: Tunde
lines: "WAEC dey come o. You don start to read?"
"I dey help my mama for shop every evening now."
"That Slim own don pass level. He get iPhone now."

talks.text: "Saturday, Wuse Market. Traders pay ₦1,000 to carry loads. Or we can stay in and read for WAEC. Or there's a football pool at the kiosk…"

choices.result: Heavy bags, heavy sun, light pockets. Lighter than before, anyway.
Tunde explains chemistry with cooking. It works.

choices.text: Bet on the Premier League at the kiosk (₦1,000)

else.toast: Arsenal. Of course it was Arsenal.

people.name: Slim
lines: "My guy, money dey this Lugbe side. Come see."
"Who school help? Ask Dangote."

talks.text: "I run a football betting pool. I need someone to collect the money in your class. 10% for you. Also, I have 'original' perfumes from Dubai."

then.toast: The vice principal finds a betting slip in your bag.
The perfume smells of kerosene by Tuesday. Customers want refunds.

choices.text: Tell Slim you're done with his runs
choices.result: Slim laughs. "You'll come back."

people.name: Mr. Ade (Maths)
lines: "Show your working, or I show you zero."
"Some of you buying 'expo'. The expo is for last year's paper."

talks.text: "I'm running free lessons after school this week. You coming?"

choices.result: Simultaneous equations finally make sense.

people.name: Bolaji
lines: "Our school has a swimming pool. And a horse. Don't ask about the horse."
"My dad says I'll study in London. I haven't even chosen a course."

talks.text: "My dad's guy usually does my assignments but he's travelling. You're smart. I'll pay."

then.toast: The teacher recognises your handwriting in Bolaji's book.

choices.result: Bolaji actually learns something. He looks almost scared by it.

choices.text: Sell him 'imported' sneakers you bought in Wuse (₦8,000)

then.toast: The sole falls off at the inter-school quiz. Bolaji knows.

people.name: Kelechi (roommate)
lines: "Who took my Indomie? I counted. There were four."
"ASUU again? I'll be thirty by the time we graduate."
"Hostel NEPA bill: ₦2,000 each. We have had light twice."

talks.text: "Guy, this hostel is a market waiting to happen. Let's do something."

choices.text: Split a provision shop in the room (₦10,000)
choices.result: Indomie, Golden Morn and noodles at midnight prices.
Your handwriting is finally worth something.

choices.text: Sign the attendance sheet for him (₦2,000)

then.toast: The lecturer counts heads. Ninety-two names, eighty-one students.

people.name: Mrs. Okafor
lines: "Shortcuts are expensive. They just send the bill later."
"Read the question twice. Answer it once."

people.name: Man in a red beret
lines: "You need protection on this campus. Think about it."
"We look after our own. Everyone else... is everyone else."

talks.text: "Protection: ₦10,000 and nobody touches you on this campus. Or you can join us, and nobody touches anybody you know."

choices.result: A receipt? No. A nod.

then.toast: A clash at the Student Union building. The school publishes names.

choices.result: You feel his eyes on your back all the way to the hostel.

people.name: Rotaract president
lines: "Charity match on Saturday! We need volunteers."
"Networking is just making friends on purpose."

talks.text: "Volunteer at our outreach this weekend?"

choices.result: You hand out textbooks at a primary school. A child asks if you're a teacher. You feel ten feet tall.

people.name: Camp soldier
lines: "CORPER! Who told you to walk? RUN!"
"4:30 a.m. tomorrow. If I see your bed made late, you'll see me."

talks.text: "Corper! You wan hold my post this night? ₦1,500. Just sit here and look serious."

then.toast: The commandant does a night round. You are holding a rifle you are not allowed to hold.

choices.result: Your khaki is now sharper than the parade itself.
"Corper, double up!"

people.name: Mammy market madam
lines: "Corper, buy fried yam! Na ₦500, no dey price."
"I don see twenty batches. Una all dey cry first week."

talks.text: "Buy fried yam and pepper sauce? ₦500."

choices.result: Hot, peppery, perfect.

people.name: Corper Chioma
lines: "I heard Nepo corpers don't even come to camp. They're 'excused'."
"If you get posted to my state, I'll show you the best spots."

talks.text: "Corper ma/sir! Let's do business. JAMB students in this town need lessons, and everyone wants cash at Mammy market."

choices.text: Run a JAMB tutorial centre together (₦20,000)
choices.result: Twenty students, one blackboard, two very tired corpers.

choices.text: Go halves on a POS machine (₦15,000)
choices.result: Withdrawals, transfers, and a lot of 'network is bad'.

then.toast: A buyer tries to use one at a federal ministry. It leads straight back to you.

people.name: Tunde
lines: "Guy! Long time. You don chop?"
"Rent for Kubwa don increase again. Landlord say na 'the economy'."
"One day we go dey Maitama. Watch."

talks.text: "I get one delivery for Wuse, my rider no show. Abeg help me carry am?"

choices.result: Tunde insists on paying you ₦5,000. "Business na business."

people.name: Slim
lines: "My guy, see my new Benz. Na 'consulting' money."
"Why you dey suffer? The format dey for you anytime."

talks.text: "Come inside, let me show you the 'office'. Just look. No commitment."

choices.result: Ring lights, laptops, three phones per person. Slim smiles: "Whenever you're ready."

people.name: Mrs. Okafor
lines: "Have you updated your CV? Update it."
"Money you didn't sweat for will run away the same way."
"Network is not begging. It's showing up, again and again."

talks.text: "I have a book you should read. Bring it back."

choices.result: "The Richest Man in Babylon". Old, but it still slaps.

choices.text: Ask for her famous efo riro recipe
choices.result: She writes it on the back of an envelope. "Blend the peppers coarse, never smooth. And don't drown the greens."

people.name: Bolaji
lines: "Bro, you look stressed. Have you tried... not being stressed?"
"Dad's people said the contract is 'sorted'. I don't even know what the contract is."

talks.text: "You came! See you, looking like money." Bolaji hands you a chapman. "Come, my father wants to meet my 'street-smart' friend. Don't mind him, he's always recruiting."

remember.what: You came to their father's party

talks.text: "My cousin's birthday on the yacht this weekend. Come. Wear something nice."

choices.result: A yacht. On Jabi Lake. You meet a CEO who 'might have something'.

people.name: Mr. Felix
lines: "Fast cash, no collateral! Your phone number is your collateral. Hehe."
"Just ₦50k to start. You'll pay it back easily. Everyone does. Eventually."

people.name: Prophet Profit
lines: "My students made 400% last month!"
"Forex is a mindset. Buy my mindset course."

talks.text: "Special offer for you only: signals for one month, ₦50,000."

choices.result: The signals: "Buy when it goes up. Sell when it goes down." That's it. That's the whole thing.

people.name: Mallam Sani (suya)
lines: "Suya hot hot! Extra yaji for you?"
"Thirty years selling suya. My children are doctors."

talks.text: "₦2,000 suya, with onions and cabbage?"

choices.result: Smoky, spicy, life-changing.

choices.text: Pay him to teach you his suya (₦15,000)
choices.result: He looks around, then shows you how he slices the beef paper-thin and what goes into his yaji. "If you open shop near me, I go find you."

people.name: Gala hawker
lines: "Gala! Fanta! Coke! Pure water!"
"Customer, buy something na. Small thing."

talks.text: "Gala and Fanta, ₦700."

choices.result: The national lunch of the hustling class.

choices.text: Ask how she makes the kunu she sells (₦3,000)
choices.result: "Millet, ginger, small clove. Leave am overnight." She laughs. "Just don't come and sell for my side."

people.name: Agbero
lines: "Owo ticket! Everybody pay!"
"Na government collect am. Which government? Our own government."

talks.text: "Oya pay your ₦300 ticket. Even if you no get motor."

choices.result: He gives you a 'receipt' written on a cigarette pack.

then.toast: You argue so well that the other drivers clap. He lets you go.

else.toast: His 'boys' arrive. You pay ₦1,000 'for wasting time'.

people.name: Mama POS
lines: "Network is bad today. Come back by evening."
"₦200 per ₦5,000 withdrawal. Banks are worse, trust me."

people.name: Oga at the Ministry
lines: "Your file? Ah, it's 'on the minister's desk'."
"Come back Monday. No, the other Monday."

talks.text: "Your file can move faster. Something for the boys, maybe ₦20,000?"

choices.result: The file moves. Into the next room.
Your file stays exactly where it is. Forever, possibly.

people.name: Corper in khaki
lines: "My allawee came three weeks late. Again."
"My PPA has me photocopying. I have a Master's."

people.name: Okada rider
lines: "Okada ban for Garki, but the police dey take 'settlement'."
"I know every shortcut for Abuja. Even the ones that don't exist."

people.name: Senator Danjuma-Adeyemi
lines: "Young person! Are you enjoying Abuja?"
"In this city, everything is negotiable. Even the law."
"My son speaks well of you. Don't make him a liar."

people.name: Halima Bello
lines: "Every building in this city has a story. Most of them are crimes."
"Off the record? Nothing is off the record."

talks.text: "You came. Good." She slides a folder across: photos of bulldozers, a list of sixty-three families. "The elder, Baba Yakubu, is still by the site in Guzape. Talk to him. Photograph the foundations if you can. Here, a press card. Security doesn't argue with the press… usually."

remember.what: You agreed to help with the Guzape story

choices.result: ABUJA DAILY · STRINGER, with your name spelt nearly right. Guzape security will let you through now.
"Integrity," she says. Then she sighs and gives you ₦20,000 for transport, and a press card.

people.name: Baba Yakubu
lines: "My father's house stood there. Right there, where the crane is."
"They said Abuja is for everybody. They didn't say everybody who?"

talks.text: "Journalist? Another one." The old man points at the rubble. "My father's house stood there. They gave us two days. The man who signed the papers drives past every morning in a black jeep." Behind him, workers pour grey slurry into a foundation. You poke it. It crumbles.

remember.what: You listened and took pictures for the press
remember.say: "Have they printed it? My people are asking."

choices.result: Twenty photos: the flattened homes, the crumbling foundation, a 50 kg cement bag you can lift with one finger.

choices.text: Give him ₦20,000 for food, then take photos

remember.what: You gave them money when they had nothing
remember.say: "You fed my family when you didn't have to. God will remember. So will I."

choices.result: He doesn't say thank you. He holds your hand for a long moment instead. Then he walks you round the site while you take twenty photos.

talks.text: He looks at your lanyard, then at you. "So the Senator sent a child to talk to me." Behind him, workers pour grey slurry into a foundation. It crumbles where it lands.

remember.what: You came with the Senator's money
remember.say: "You again. Have you come to buy something else?"

choices.result: He takes it. What choice does he have? Then he spits on the ground beside your shoe.

choices.text: Put the envelope away and just listen

remember.what: You listened when you were sent to silence them
remember.say: "The Senator's child who listened. Strange times."

choices.result: He talks for an hour. Somewhere between his story and the crumbling concrete, you take out your phone and start taking pictures.

people.name: Kemi
lines: "Tom-Tom, ₦10. Chin-chin, ₦20. Credit is for your father."
"My mummy says I'll be a big woman in the market."

talks.text: "You want sweets or you want business? I have stock. You have customers in your row."

choices.result: Menthol and happiness.

choices.text: Go into business with Kemi: you sell her stock in your row
Ask Kemi to teach you how to haggle
choices.result: "Never say your price first." She is nine. She is right.

people.name: Mama Put
lines: "Rice and stew, ₦100. Meat is extra, and meat is small."
"Pikin, you dey hungry? Your face don tell me."

talks.text: "You want to eat, or you want to work? I have puff-puff and I have plates."

choices.text: Buy puff-puff wholesale and sell it at break
choices.result: Twenty puff-puff, twenty customers, ₦900 profit.
Your hands smell of palm oil for a week.
"I go write am for my book." There is always a book.

people.name: Mallam Garba (kiosk)
lines: "Recharge card, sweet, biscuit, Bournvita. No credit today, come tomorrow."
"Small business is the mother of big business."

talks.text: "You want to work? I need a boy or girl on Saturdays. Or buy from me wholesale and sell in your school."

choices.text: Buy wholesale and sell in school
choices.result: Biscuits by the carton, sold by the packet.
You learn every recharge card PIN pattern in Nigeria.
₦50 on every ₦1,000 card. It adds up.

people.name: Senior Chuka
lines: "Junior, why are you walking like you own this school?"
"In my time, juniors respected seniors." He is in SS3.

talks.text: "Junior! Bring my food from the dining hall every day and you'll be under my protection."

choices.result: Nobody else touches you. Chuka touches your food.
"Okay. We'll see."

choices.text: Report his bullying to the house master

then.toast: Chuka finds out. Your shin finds out too.

people.name: Chairman Tobi
lines: "Hustle is hustle. Don't judge me."
"My client in Texas thinks I'm a doctor. I'm a doctor of format."

talks.text: "Your bank account dey work? I need to receive ₦500,000. I'll give you 20%. Or buy my 'format' PDF."

choices.text: Lend him your account for a 20% cut

then.toast: The money was traced. Your account is frozen and the school is informed.

choices.result: Twenty pages of lies, with spelling mistakes.
"Okay o. When you're tired of suffering, you know my room."

people.name: Aunty Bisi (food seller)
lines: "Jollof is ready! Jollof is always ready."
"Students owe me more money than the government."

talks.text: "I need someone to deliver food to the hostels at night. ₦100 a plate."

choices.result: Sixty plates, four hostels, one happy Aunty Bisi.

choices.text: Collect her debts from students for a 20% cut
choices.result: You discover who owes whom on this campus. It's everyone.
Jollof heals.

people.name: POS Mama
lines: "Network is bad. Network is always bad."
"Withdraw ₦5,000, charge ₦200. No argument."

talks.text: "Corper, help me run my stand at night. Or sell me your allawee alert in advance, I'll give you cash now."

choices.text: Run her POS stand at night (₦5,000)
choices.result: Cash, alerts and a lot of shouting.

choices.text: Sell your next allawee in advance (₦60,000 now)
choices.result: You'll get ₦77,000 next month. She'll get it instead.

choices.text: Use her stand to 'reverse' a transfer on a stranger

then.toast: The stranger is a corper from your platoon. He reports you.
